card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces std::format support at CMake configure time. This unblocks the adoption of C++20 std::format across the codebase and prepares the build system for C++23. CI environments are updated accordingly, including upgrading the previous-releases runner to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-builds to GCC 14 runtime libraries. Users building on older distributions lacking GCC 13 will need to use Clang or alternative toolchain packages.
changed_since_previous: Removed the reference to #36033, added removal of redundant GCC 13 instructions from doc/build-windows.md, and dropped obsolete -Werror flags from the previous-releases CI script.
evidence: PR description: '(For this bump, only C++20 std::format will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23.)'
Commit a0f8d1aeff: 'bench: refactor: tfm->std::format - Make an example replacement to use std::format. New code can use this now, but old code can probably stay as-is for now.'
problem: Developers cannot use C++20 std::format in the codebase because GCC 12 lacks support for <format>, delaying adoption of modern standard library formatting and eventual transition to C++23.

risk.why: A mistake in compiler feature checks or cross-compilation flags could prevent builds or CI from succeeding on supported platforms.

summary: Bumps the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and adds a CMake configure-time check requiring C++20 <format> support. It updates CI environments to GCC 13+ (upgrading the native previous-releases test runner to Ubuntu 24.04 and NetBSD cross-compilation to GCC 14 libraries), drops a redundant Windows build note, and converts a wallet migration benchmark from tinyformat to std::format as an example.
